newsitem.title: UK: Oil spill tanker Sea Empress relaunched.
newsitem.headline: Oil spill tanker Sea Empress relaunched.

text.p: The ill-fated tanker Sea Empress, which last year spilt 70,000 tonnes of oil off south Wales, put to sea again on Wednesday after undergoing millions of pounds worth of repairs.
The 147,273 dwt vessel, renamed the Sea Spirit, left dry dock after being repaired at the Harland & Wolff shipyard in Belfast.
It will undergo sea trials in the north Atlantic before reentering service.
A Harland & Wolff spokesman said, "A lot of industry experts say it was the largest conventional ship repair ever undertaken, and the most difficult.
"We have done it on time, within budget, the owners are delighted with the vessel and we are feeling very pleased with ourselves."
The spillage off Milford Haven in February 1996 was one of Britain's worst such disasters and occurred in an enviromentally highly sensitive area.
The ship is operated by Glasgow-based Acomarit on behalf of owners Seatankers Management, based in Cyprus.
